```javascript
test('create then get',async()=>{
  const c=await callTool('note_create',{title:'A',body:'B'});
  const id=c.content[0].text.match(/n\d+/)[0];
  const g=await callTool('note_get',{note_id:id});

});
```

The test:
1. Creates a note with title 'A' and body 'B'
2. Extracts the id from the text using regex `n\d+`
3. Gets the note with that id
4. Asserts the text contains 'A' (the title)

So the response text needs to contain something matching `n\d+` (like `n1`, `n42`, etc.).

```javascript
test('lists two tools',async()=>assert.equal((await listTools()).length,2));
```

This test expects exactly 2 tools.

Let me think about the design:

1. **listTools()**: Returns an array of tool descriptors with:
   - `name`
   - `description`
   - `inputSchema` with `type`, `properties`, `required`, and `additionalProperties: false`

2. **callTool(name, args)**: Returns an object with:
   - `content`: array of content objects, each with `type: 'text'` and `text`
   - Should throw errors for invalid inputs or unknown tools

3. **Storage**: In-memory (use a Map)

4. **ID generation**: Stable, generated. Looking at the regex `/n\d+/`, the IDs should look like `n1`, `n42`, etc. I need to make them stable - perhaps using a counter that's consistent.

Let me think about what "stable generated ids" means - it could mean:
- Predictable (counter-based)
- Stable across calls (don't regenerate)
- Uniquely generated

I'll use a counter starting from 1, incremented each time, so they look like `n1`, `n2`, etc.

Let me write the server.mjs:

```javascript
const notes = new Map();
let nextId = 1;

const tools = [
  {
    name: 'note_create',
    description: 'Create a new note with a title and body.',
    inputSchema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        title: { type: 'string', description: 'The title of the note (non-empty).' },
        body: { type: 'string', description: 'The body of the note (non-empty).' }
      },
      required: ['title', 'body'],
      additionalProperties: false
    }
  },
  {
    name: 'note_get',
    description: 'Get a previously created note by its id.',
    inputSchema: {
      type: 'object',
      properties: {
        note_id: { type: 'string', description: 'The id of the note to retrieve.' }
      },
      required: ['note_id'],
      additionalProperties: false
    }
  }
];

export async function listTools() {
  return tools;
}

export async function callTool(name, args) {
  if (name === 'note_create') {
    const { title, body } = args || {};
    if (typeof title !== 'string' || title.length === 0) {
      throw new Error('Invalid arguments: title must be a non-empty string');
    }
    if (typeof body !== 'string' || body.length === 0) {
      throw new Error('Invalid arguments: body must be a non-empty string');
    }
    const id = `n${nextId++}`;
    notes.set(id, { id, title, body });
    return {
      content: [{ type: 'text', text: `Created note ${id} with title "${title}"` }]
    };
  }
  if (name === 'note_get') {
    const { note_id } = args || {};
    if (typeof note_id !== 'string' || note_id.length === 0) {
      throw new Error('Invalid arguments: note_id must be a non-empty string');
    }
    const note = notes.get(note_id);
    if (!note) {
      throw new Error(`Unknown note_id: ${note_id}`);
    }
    return {
      content: [{ type: 'text', text: `Note ${note.id}\nTitle: ${note.title}\nBody: ${note.body}` }]
    };
  }
  throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${name}`);
}
```

- `note_get`: validates non-empty `note_id`, looks up the note, returns its id/title/body, or throws if not found
- Any other name → throws `Unknown tool: <name>`
